ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
DOCKER_PLATFORM:
- linux/amd64
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
ADAPY (ADA, Advanced Design & Analysis) is a python library for structural
analysis and design. It reads and writes common CAD and FEM formats and can
build, visualise and run analyses on structural models.

Installing this package also provides the `ada` command-line tool. Run
`ada --help` for the full list of subcommands; these include `ada convert`
(convert between supported CAD/FEM formats), `ada view` (open a model in
Ada Studio, the built-in web app) and `ada serve` (run the REST API or
worker process).
about.summary: ADA (Advanced Design & Analysis) - a python library for structural analysis and design, plus the `ada` command-line tool

about.description:
A native desktop window for Ada Studio, the web app that ships with ada-py.
`ada desktop` starts the local viewer server from the installed ada-py and
opens it in this window, with native pop-out windows, remembered window
positions and a native 3D mouse reader. Requires the Microsoft Edge WebView2
runtime, which ships with current Windows.
about.summary: Desktop window for Ada Studio, launched with `ada desktop`

name: ada-py-desktop
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: ada-py
  version: "0.147.0"
  python_min: "3.11"

recipe:
  name: ${{ name }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/Krande/adapy/archive/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: d688f019f43954c5bee7ea85c26c86c955c01bd192a3ae0c7b3a6afae2b0e39b

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}-core
    build:
      noarch: python
      # The noarch outputs are built once, on linux. The Windows job exists only
      # for the -desktop output; building these there too would upload the same
      # noarch files twice.
      skip: win
      script: python -m pip install . --no-deps -vv
      python:
        entry_points:
          - ada=ada_cli.main:main
    requirements:
      host:
        - pip
        - setuptools
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
    about:
      description: |
        The core package without dependencies of ADAPY (ADA, Advanced Design & Analysis), a python library for structural analysis and design.

        This output ships the `ada` command-line entry point; most of its
        subcommands need the full `ada-py` package to be installed as well.

  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}
    build:
      noarch: python
      skip: win
      # The `ada` console script, declared here as well as on `ada-py-core`, so that
      # installing only the metapackage gets you the CLI.
      #
      # It works without this output having a build script or a single file of its own:
      # for `noarch: python`, `entry_points` is not compiled into the package, it is
      # recorded in `info/link.json` and the script is generated by the installer at link
      # time. The module it imports only has to be importable *then*, and
      # `pin_subpackage("ada-py-core", exact=True)` below guarantees it is. Verified
      # locally against rattler-build 0.49.0: the metapackage's link.json carries the
      # entry point, `bin/ada` appears in an environment that asks only for `ada-py`, and
      # `pixi global install ada-py` reports `exposes: ada`.
      #
      # That last one is the point. `pixi global install ada-py` exposes the executables
      # of the package it was asked for, and a metapackage with no files has none -- so
      # the CLI silently did not arrive unless the user knew to name `ada-py-core` too.
      python:
        entry_points:
          - ada=ada_cli.main:main

    requirements:
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - numpy
        - hdf5
        - h5py
        - ifcopenshell
        - bcf-client
        # The CAD kernel. ada-cpp rather than pythonocc-core, because the geometry
        # layer's own path through it is the native one: ada.cad's backend registry
        # prefers ada-cpp when both are present, and the tessellation, STEP/IFC and
        # topology verbs it exposes are what adapy calls.
        #
        # This is also what lets the closure move to OCCT 8: pythonocc-core's newest
        # build is 7.9.3 and pins occt ==7.9.3, so requiring it holds every consumer
        # of ada-py on the 7.9 line regardless of what they themselves need.
        #
        # pythonocc-core is NOT gone, only un-required. `ada.occ` is unchanged and
        # ADAPY_CAD_BACKEND=occ still selects it; installing pythonocc-core alongside
        # is supported and is how anything reaching for an OCC capability ada-cpp does
        # not cover yet -- curved-face imprint is the live one -- keeps working.
        - ada-cpp
        - python-gmsh
        - pyquaternion
        # ada.api.animations / scene_converter build on trimesh's private glTF
        # internals (_data_append, the buffer_postprocessor bufferView
        # insertion-order contract), which the 5.0 major bump breaks. Upstream
        # locks/tests against 4.12.2; cap below 5 until adapy migrates.
        - trimesh >=5
        # No direct occt entry: it arrived with pythonocc-core and adapy links nothing
        # against it itself. ada-cpp carries the version it was built for, which is the
        # only one that can be right.
        - send2trash
        - meshio
        - websockets
        - plotly
        - python-kaleido
        - pydantic
        - ipywidgets
        - jupyterlab
        - pyparsing
        - pyglfw
        - pygfx
        - python-flatbuffers
        - openpyxl
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("ada-py-core", exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - ada
          pip_check: false
          python_version: ${{ python_min }}.*
      - files:
          source:
            - tests
            - files
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - pytest
            - pytest-cov
            - pytest-asyncio
            - calculix
            - libgl-devel
            - mesalib
            - xorg-libxdamage
            - xorg-libxxf86vm
            - xorg-libxext
        script:
          # test_no_call_site_reimplements_the_env_parse greps the upstream src/ tree, which is not
          # part of the test files copied here; it is a repo lint, not a package test.
          # test_the_gate_can_actually_fail (assets layering gate AND clash vocabulary gate) uses
          # `git grep` to prove the forbidden tokens are findable -- the copied test-files tree
          # here has no .git of its own, so git grep searches the feedstock checkout around it and
          # silently finds nothing instead of erroring; a repo lint, not a package test. Both
          # gates read the installed package instead from the next adapy release, and these two
          # deselects can go then.
          # test_committed_frontend_fixture_is_current imports tools/gen_beam_solids_compact_fixture.py,
          # which lives outside the tests/ and files/ trees copied here.
          - pytest tests --ignore=tests/fem --ignore=tests/profiling --ignore=tests/examples --ignore=tests/full/frontend --ignore=tests/comms/rest --cov=ada --cov-report=xml --ignore=tests/core/visit/plotting/test_easy_plotly.py --deselect 
            tests/core/cad/test_tess_env_defaults.py::test_no_call_site_reimplements_the_env_parse --deselect tests/core/assets/test_layering_gate.py::test_the_gate_can_actually_fail --deselect tests/core/clash/test_vocabulary_gate.py::test_the_gate_can_actually_fail --deselect 
            tests/core/fem/results/test_beam_compact.py::test_committed_frontend_fixture_is_current

  # The desktop window for Ada Studio: a small native shell (Tauri, using the
  # system WebView2) that `ada desktop` launches against the local viewer server
  # it starts from this same environment. It embeds no frontend -- the viewer
  # bundle already ships in ada-py -- and links nothing from Python, so it is a
  # plain platform binary next to the noarch packages above. Windows only for now.
  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}-desktop
    build:
      skip: not win
      script:
        file: build-desktop
      dynamic_linking:
        # A Windows API set DLL (WebView2 / WinRT error reporting): part of the OS,
        # never a conda package. rattler-build's own system list doesn't cover it,
        # and error_overlinking would otherwise fail the build on it.
        missing_dso_allowlist:
          - "**/api-ms-win-core-winrt-*.dll"
    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('rust') }}
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - cargo-bundle-licenses
      run:
        # Not pin_subpackage: ada-py is built on the linux job, not alongside this one.
        # `ada desktop` (in ada-py) and this binary are released together.
        - ada-py ==${{ version }}
    tests:
      # A contents check, not `ada-desktop --version`: a script test installs the run
      # dependencies, and ada-py at this exact version is built by the linux job of
      # the same run, so it is not on the channel yet when this job tests.
      - package_contents:
          bin:
            - ada-desktop
    about:
      summary: Desktop window for Ada Studio, launched with `ada desktop`
      description: |
        A native desktop window for Ada Studio, the web app that ships with ada-py.
        `ada desktop` starts the local viewer server from the installed ada-py and
        opens it in this window, with native pop-out windows, remembered window
        positions and a native 3D mouse reader. Requires the Microsoft Edge WebView2
        runtime, which ships with current Windows.
      license: GPL-3.0-or-later
      license_file:
        - LICENSE
        - THIRDPARTY.yml
